name: Reverin
description: Reverin is not a traditional pharmaceutical in the conventional sense — it is a SNT-derived neural contrast agent that, when administered before sleep, coats active REM-stage neural pathways in a BCI-readable bioelectric signature, allowing the user's brain-computer interface to capture, encode, and store dream content as playable sensory files. The resulting recordings (.rvr format) capture visual, auditory, tactile, and emotional content with approximately 70-85% fidelity to the original dream experience and can be replayed, edited, or shared.
effects: Emotional content encoding alongside sensory data
Dreams can be replayed, edited, and shared post-sleep
Enhanced dream recall even without playback
side_effects: Neural contrast agent causes mild inflammation at BCI interface site with repeated use
Some users report feeling 'observed' during dreams, altering content
Privacy risk: .rvr files are highly personal and frequently stolen or leaked
Occasionally captures content user did not consciously experience — 'sub-surface' material
duration: Active during sleep (contrast agent metabolizes in 10-12 hours)
cultural_context: Dream recording has spawned an entire subculture and economy. 'Dreamcasters' — people with particularly vivid or creative Oneiravast-enhanced dreams — use Reverin to record and sell their dream content as immersive entertainment. There is a thriving black market for celebrity dream recordings, for erotic dream content, and more disturbingly, for trauma recordings — people paying to experience genuine fear, grief, or loss in a controlled context. Legal questions around dream content ownership are completely unresolved.
story_hooks: A political figure's Reverin-recorded dreams have been stolen and contain information that could destroy several careers and implicate a corponation in something catastrophic — the files are on the market and multiple parties are hunting for them.

A grief-tech startup is approaching bereaved families with an offer: if their deceased loved one ever used Reverin, those archived dreams can be sold back to them. The crew has been hired to determine whether the company is also manufacturing fake 'loved one' content.
